nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice-site variants in PPFIBP1 (12p11.22; NM_003622.4) are predicted to cause nonsense-mediated decay and loss of liprin-beta1. Nine distinct variants were found in the 12 founding families, three of them recurrent; a later Pakistani family carried a further homozygous nonsense variant, c.466C>T p.(Gln156*). The most upstream truncating variant (p.Arg135*) and a canonical splice-site variant were associated with milder courses, possibly through alternative transcripts or residual splicing. A homozygous SAM-domain missense variant, p.(Gly726Val), in a fetus with intracranial calcifications is predicted to destabilize the SAM2-SAM3 interface.

nodes.description: Liprin-beta1 homodimerizes and heterodimerizes with the liprin-alpha proteins through its C-terminal SAM domains. Liprin-alpha proteins are presynaptic active-zone scaffolds, and liprin-alpha2 binds liprin-beta1 and the neurodevelopmental scaffold CASK simultaneously, forming a ternary complex. Loss of liprin-beta1 is therefore expected to impair liprin-mediated assembly of synaptic protein complexes. That the complex is disrupted in patient cells has not been shown.

nodes.description: Bilateral calcifications in the periventricular white matter, and often the basal ganglia, were present in every individual who had a CT scan, together with periventricular leukoencephalopathy and white-matter loss that progressed on serial imaging in two individuals. Fetal autopsy showed macrocalcification and rare necrotic foci calcifying in the germinative and periventricular zones. The mechanism linking loss of liprin-beta1 to this tissue injury is unknown, so the node has no upstream edge.

nodes.description: C. elegans hlb-1 (PPFIBP1 ortholog) mutants mislocalize the synaptic vesicle marker SNB-1, have enlarged synaptic sites, reduced pharyngeal pumping and altered locomotion, and are resistant to the acetylcholinesterase inhibitor aldicarb while remaining levamisole-sensitive, indicating reduced presynaptic acetylcholine release. A light-evoked increase in head-tip acceleration in a knockout strain overlaps with existing worm seizure models. How this presynaptic defect produces human epilepsy has not been shown.
